claim: pw4 located the whole skeleton gap in the epilogue: noepi saves 2.3 µs at m=1 and 5.2 µs at m=32 against base, and noepi+nopro sits at the pure stream. pw5 splits that epilogue into its parts with probes (reductions, fence, counter, finalize, vector width, fence scope). It also moves the epilogue off the critical path on the real m<=32 paths. Two extra epilogue warps take each finished n-block from a double-buffered smem staging area and reduce, fence, count and finalize it while the 16 consumer warps stream the next n-block. That needs at least 2 n-blocks per CTA. pw4's grid gave pooler exactly 1 (NG = NB = 16 at BN 256), so the overlapped paths are registered at >= 2 and >= 4 n-blocks per CTA. Only the last n-block's epilogue stays exposed. Prediction: the overlapped skeleton lands within ~1 µs of noepi at both m. With compute nearly hidden (pw3), the full GEMM then lands ~1.5-2 µs above pure, about 13.5-14 judge µs at m=1/16/32 on pooler and qkv.
target_shapes: pooler m=1, m=16, m=32 and qkv m=1/16/32 with pw-b16t* (overlapped): within-run in-prepare at or below pure + 2 µs; at or below pw4's b16 times
unpooler n=1024 (m <= 8): pw-b8t1 (pw4's winner there), unchanged
kill_if: Kill the overlapped epilogue if overlap and overlap-nb4 are not at least 1 µs below full at m=32 within the run, or if nored is not below overlap (then the epilogue warps themselves are the bottleneck and need a different reduction scheme, e.g. cluster/DSMEM partial sums). Kill the whole m<=32 bulk family if pw-b16t* still loses to torch on pooler m=1 and m=32 after the overlap. r6 then keeps m<=32.

probe_plan.where: prepare(), after compile and before the bake-off, <= 15 s, try/except, selects nothing. Kernel: the L1 skeleton (producer streams W, consumers only wait/arrive) of the 16-consumer-warp bulk kernel. pooler (50 MB packed, BN 256 -> 16 n-blocks), m=1 and m=32. One line each: 'PROBE epi m=<m> <name> grid=<g> <us>'. Plus 'pure' (pw2's bulk stream) as the in-run reference, and 'PW epi-config' lines (NG, KS, grid, n-blocks/CTA, stages/CTA, bytes/CTA, smem, ST) for full, overlap and overlap-nb4. 23 PROBE lines + 6 config lines.
probe_plan.reference_note: The judge drifts about 10% between runs, so only same-run differences are meaningful. pw4 same-run figures: pure 18.7; m=1 base 20.4, noepi 18.1; m=32 base 25.1, noepi 19.9.

lines.pure: pw2's pure bulk stream (16 KB x 4, 132 CTAs, 1 consumer warp). Prediction: about 18.7 (pw4) ±10% drift.
lines.full: = pw4 base: per-n-block red.v4 flush by the consumers, then per-thread __threadfence, consumer-only named barrier, atomicAdd counters, serial finalize by the last arriver. Prediction: m=1 base+0, m=32 base+0 (20.4 / 25.1 in pw4's run).
lines.noepi: No flush, fence, count or finalize. Prediction: m=1 -2.3, m=32 -5.2 vs full.
lines.redonly: Flush reductions only (no fence, no counter, no finalize). Isolates the red.v4 traffic plus its drain at CTA exit. Prediction: m=1 full-1.8 (about 0.5 above noepi), m=32 full-3.5 (4.2 MB of reductions at the tail, about 1.5 above noepi).
lines.red+fence: Adds the per-thread __threadfence after the flush. The fence waits for this thread's reductions to be acknowledged, so it exposes the red latency. Prediction: +0.5 at m=1, +0.8 at m=32 over redonly.
lines.red+fence+cnt: Adds the counter atomics (no finalize). Prediction: +0.3 over red+fence.
lines.fin512: full, with the finalize batched (4 independent 16 B ld.cg per thread before the stores) over all 512 consumer threads. Prediction: finalize -0.5 at m=1, -1.0 at m=32 vs full.
lines.redv1: full with scalar red.global.add.f32 (4x the ops). Prediction: +0.3 at m=1, +1.5 at m=32 vs full. If it is near full, the cost is the latency/drain, not the reduction throughput.
lines.fencecta: Consumer-only bar.sync, then ONE fence.acq_rel.gpu by one thread, instead of 512 per-thread fences. Prediction: -0.3 to -0.5 vs full (all 512 fences wait on the same outstanding reductions).
lines.overlap: The pw5 design at L1, >= 2 n-blocks per CTA (pooler grid 8x15): consumers stage, 2 epilogue warps reduce, fence, count and finalize behind them. Prediction: m=1 about noepi+0.6, m=32 about noepi+1.5 (the last n-block's epilogue and the larger K split remain).
lines.overlap-nb4: Same with >= 4 n-blocks per CTA (4x29): a smaller exposed tail per CTA but about 2x the reductions (m=32: 15 MB). Prediction: m=1 below overlap by ~0.3; m=32 about overlap (more reduction traffic offsets the shorter tail).
lines.nored: overlap without the global reductions (staging, fence, counter, finalize kept). Upper bound of the overlapped design. Prediction: about noepi+0.3.

epilogue_design.warps: Per CTA: warps 0-15 consumers (16 x 1 row tile of BN 256), warp 16 producer, warps 17-18 epilogue (EW = 2): 608 threads. ptxas: b16t1 69, b16t2 86, b16t4 89 regs, 0 spill, so 1 CTA/SM fits in registers.
epilogue_design.buffers: Two staging buffers of FRAG = RTB*TT*32 float4 in fragment order (identical to the workspace layout): 8 KB each at m<=8, 16 KB at m=16, 32 KB at m=32. They sit between the W ring + barriers and the x slice. smem per CTA (pooler): 128 KB (m<=8, ring 4 x 24 KB), 146-160 KB (m=16, ring 4), 157-201 KB (m=32, ring dropped to 3). The grid chooser and the launcher include the staging bytes.
epilogue_design.barriers: mbarriers sfull[2] (count 16, one arrive per consumer warp after __syncwarp) and sempty[2] (count EW). A consumer finishing n-block i (i-th of its CTA) waits sempty[i&1] with parity ((i>>1)-1)&1 when i >= 2. It then st.shared.v4's its fragments into buffer i&1, zeroes its accumulators, arrives sfull[i&1], and continues streaming. Epilogue warp loop i = 0..NBR-1: wait sfull[i&1] with parity (i>>1)&1, read the fragments (ld.shared.v4), arrive sempty[i&1] (the buffer is free as soon as it is read), then the proven split-K ordering: red.global.add.v4 -> per-thread __threadfence -> epilogue-only named barrier (bar.sync 2, 64) -> one atomicAdd on cnt[nb] -> bar.sync 2 -> if last: __threadfence, batched ld.cg / st.cg zero / bf16 store of the n-block (8 loads in flight per thread), cnt[nb] = 0. KS == 1: the epilogue warps convert and store bf16 from smem directly, with no reductions or counters.
epilogue_design.exit_order: The producer exits after its last issue. The consumers exit after parking their last n-block (no CTA-wide barrier after the prologue). The epilogue warps exit last, after the last n-block's count/finalize, so only that n-block's epilogue is exposed.
epilogue_design.grid: Overlapped paths use _pw_grid(..., nbr_min): NG <= NB/nbr_min. pw-b16t* use nbr_min 2 and pw-b16t*n4 use 4 (pooler 8x15 and 4x29; qkv 4x29 and 2x57; unpooler 16x8 / 8x15 at m >= 16). Reductions rise with KS: m=32 pooler 7.9 MB at nbr 2, 15.2 MB at nbr 4.
epilogue_design.m128: Left as in pw4. The tm kernel has one n-block per CTA (grid NB x KS), so an overlapped epilogue would have nothing after it to hide behind; only a multi-n-block tm grid would benefit, which is a different design.
epilogue_design.unchanged: Codec, fragment maps, escapes, x-stationary prologue, producer first-issue and escape prefetch (pw4). Probe switches are compiled only into the PRB=1 probe instances; the path instances reject non-zero flags.

paths: pw-b16t1 / pw-b16t1n4 (m 1, 8), pw-b16t2 / n4 (m 16), pw-b16t4 / n4 (m 32): overlapped, four BF16 layers. pw-b8t1 (EW 0): unpooler n=1024 only (m 1, 8). pw-tm, pw-tms (m 128). The 8-warp m>=16 paths and pw4's non-overlapped b16 paths are dropped. Router, m=256 and odd m stay on the fallback.
instantiations: 11: b16t1, b16t2, b16t4 (EW 2), b8t1 (EW 0), tm, s16t1, s16t4 (EW 0, PRB), s16t1E, s16t4E (EW 2, PRB), pw_probe_bulk, pw_probe_empty.
register_budget_ptxas: nvcc 12.8 sm_90a -O3, all 0 stack and 0 spill: b16t1 69, b16t2 86, b16t4 89, b8t1 65, tm 150, s16t1 48, s16t4 58, s16t1E 70, s16t4E 80, pw_probe_bulk 22, pw_probe_empty 10.
compile_check: 11/11 kernels spill-free (above). The full CUDA_SRC compiles with -std=c++20 against the minimal torch mock with no errors or warnings.
verification_done_offline: emu_pw5.py (scratchpad). (1) The pw2 emulator with the n-block flush replaced by the pw5 data path: consumers stage every lane's fragment into buffer (i & 1) at the fragment index; the epilogue walks idx in kernel order (bf16 store for KS == 1, otherwise reductions); then count and finalize. It asserts no unwritten staging slot is read. b16t1 (2 n-blocks per CTA, uneven K), b16t2 (4 n-blocks, so the buffers are reused, KS 1), b16t4 (3 n-blocks, odd m=27, KS 2) and b16t4 (NG 2, KS 3) are all bit-exact on one-hot rows and fp64-exact on random rows. (2) 1620 randomized schedules of one CTA (W ring + consumers + staging double buffer + epilogue warps; ST 2-4, 1-5 stages per n-block, 1-9 n-blocks, NWC/EW 2/1, 4/2, 16/2): no deadlock, no W read before fill or overwrite before release, and the epilogue always reads exactly n-block i. Removing the consumers' sempty wait is caught in 56/60 runs. Lint ok; cpu-check --official 9/9.
risks: The overlapped paths need >= 2 n-blocks per CTA, which raises KS. At m=32 that is 8-15 MB of reductions instead of 4. If L2 reduction throughput (about 2.5 TB/s, pw2) competes with the HBM stream, overlap may not win at m=32; the n4/n2 pair and the probe lines show it.

Two epilogue warps hold the reductions for a whole n-block (m=32: 2048 v4 reductions per CTA per n-block, 32 per thread). If they fall behind, consumers stall on sempty; that is visible as overlap ≈ full.
The epilogue warps' __threadfence still waits for their own reductions, but that is now off the consumers' path. The last n-block's epilogue is still exposed.
Log: about 30 PROBE/config + about 45 PW build + about 150 BAKE/PICK lines, about 10 KB. Prepare: 9 paths; m=1 one-hot validation for 3 paths x 4 layers, about 10 s.
